characters.name: Carbon
characters.text: Character: Carbon; Core quirk: The host who always keeps exactly four commitments. Builds chains and rings with its own kind. Its mood depends on how it holds hands (see Carbon's moods).; Encodes: Valency 4; catenation; hybridisation; In reactions: Skeleton of every molecule. Becomes a carbocation, carbanion or radical when a partner leaves with or without the electrons (H1, H2, X2, C5).; Never: Never keeps five partners; five partial bonds exist only for an instant in the SN2 transition state (X1).

characters.name: Hydrogen
characters.text: Character: Hydrogen; Core quirk: The most transferable guest. Leaves in whatever form the moment demands: as a bare proton (H⁺), a lone atom (H•) or with a pair of electrons (H⁻). Gets more nervous (acidic) the harder its neighbour pulls.; Encodes: Acidity depends on the atom it is bonded to; hydride transfer; hyperconjugation; In reactions: H⁺ attacks first in HBr addition (H2) and joins the carbon that already has more hydrogens: "jiske paas zyada, use aur" (Markovnikov). H• is stolen by Cl• (H1) and delivered last under peroxide (H3). H⁻ is handed over by LiAlH₄/NaBH₄ (C3) and passed between two aldehydes in Cannizzaro (C7). Leaves as H⁺ to restore the benzene ring (H9). α-H next to C=O is restless and leaves to base (C5, C6). C–H next to a carbocation lends support (hyperconjugation).; Never: Never released as H₂ by sodium from an alkane or alkene; only acidic H (O–H, ≡C–H) does that (O1, H7). Never leaves a ring as hydride.

characters.name: Oxygen
characters.text: Character: Oxygen; Core quirk: Possessive, with two free hands (lone pairs). Pulls shared electrons towards herself, grabs H⁺ readily, shares her lone pair generously with a ring.; Encodes: Electronegativity 3.44; two lone pairs; +R on rings, −I always; In reactions: In C=O she pulls the π pair, leaving carbon exposed (δ+) for nucleophiles (C1). In –OH she refuses to leave until she gets an H⁺, then leaves happily as water (O2, O3). As phenoxide she spreads her negative charge round the ring, which is why phenol is acidic (P1). In esterification the alcohol's oxygen stays in the ester; the acid's –OH leaves (O6).; Never: Never leaves as OH⁻ in substitution. Never lets go of an aryl carbon: phenol's C–O never breaks with HCl, anisole + HI never gives iodobenzene (O8, P6).

characters.name: Nitrogen
characters.text: Character: Nitrogen; Core quirk: The generous donor with one gift (lone pair). Gives it more readily than oxygen, unless someone else is already holding it.; Encodes: Electronegativity 3.04, one lone pair; base and nucleophile; In reactions: Attacks as a nucleophile: on alkyl halides (A9), on NO⁺ in diazotisation (A5), on sulphur in Hinsberg (A4), on carbene in carbylamine (A3). In aniline the gift is shared with the ring (weaker base, strong ring activator). In amides it is shared with C=O (neutral; N–H becomes acidic, A1, A2). When protonated it becomes –NH₃⁺ and turns germophobe (see seating rules). As N₂ in a diazonium salt it is the best leaver of all, leaving as gas (A5, A6).; Never: Never lets aniline undergo Friedel–Crafts: it handcuffs AlCl₃ (A8). Never stays as aliphatic diazonium: leaves at once as N₂ (A5).

characters.name: Fluorine
characters.text: Character: Fluorine; Core quirk: The most possessive character of all. Once attached, never lets go. Too violent to invite directly.; Encodes: Highest electronegativity (3.98); strongest C–X bond; strongest −I; In reactions: Brought in only indirectly: Swarts (AgF, Hg₂F₂, CoF₂, SbF₃, X4) or via diazonium + HBF₄ (A6). Its pull makes FCH₂COOH the strongest of the haloacetic acids.; Never: Never a good leaving group. Never added by direct fluorination in a controlled story.

characters.name: Chlorine
characters.text: Character: Chlorine; Core quirk: Aggressive but unselective. As a radical grabs any hydrogen it meets; as a substituent, slow to leave.; Encodes: Reactive radical; moderate leaving group; C–Cl on a ring has partial double-bond character; In reactions: Radical chain on alkanes, giving mixtures (H1). With AlCl₃/FeCl₃ becomes Cl⁺ and attacks benzene (H9). In sunlight attacks toluene's side chain; with FeCl₃ attacks the ring (main tab). On a ring it is "grumpy but polite" (see seating rules).; Never: Never leaves a benzene ring easily: needs 623 K and 300 atm (X7). Never selective between 1°, 2°, 3° H.

characters.name: Bromine
characters.text: Character: Bromine; Core quirk: The shapeshifter. Plays four different roles depending on the reaction, and always announces itself: its red-brown colour vanishes when it reacts with a double bond.; Encodes: Polarisable Br₂; Br⁻ stable anion; Br• radical; good leaving group; In reactions: Electrophile (Brδ+) adding to C=C (H4) and attacking phenol or aniline (P2, A8). Nucleophile Br⁻ completing HBr addition (H2). Radical Br• with peroxide, adding first to the end carbon (H3), and choosy: prefers 3° H. Leaving group in SN1/SN2 (X1, X2) and from nitrogen in Hofmann (A1).; Never: Never reverses Markovnikov without peroxide. Never switches to the radical role with HCl or HI.

characters.name: Iodine
characters.text: Character: Iodine; Core quirk: The laid-back one. Leaves without a fight; lazy at attacking benzene.; Encodes: Weakest C–X bond; best leaving group; I₂ a weak electrophile; I⁻ a strong nucleophile; In reactions: Leaves most easily in SN1/SN2. I⁻ cracks ethers, attacking the smaller alkyl group (O8). Swaps in for Cl/Br in acetone (Finkelstein, X4). Replaces N₂ without copper (A6). Ends up as yellow CHI₃ in the iodoform test (C6).; Never: Never iodinates benzene on its own: the reaction runs backwards unless HNO₃ or HIO₄ removes HI.

characters.name: Sulphur
characters.text: Character: Sulphur; Core quirk: The reversible committer. Joins a ring as –SO₃H but can be asked to leave. As SOCl₂, the clean exit artist.; Encodes: Sulphonation is reversible; SOCl₂ by-products (SO₂, HCl) are gases; In reactions: SO₃ attacks benzene (H9). SOCl₂ turns –OH into –Cl and leaves nothing behind (O3, C9). In C₆H₅SO₂Cl it is the target the amine's nitrogen attacks (A4).; Never: Never leaves solid or liquid by-products in a SOCl₂ reaction.

characters.name: Phosphorus
characters.text: Character: Phosphorus; Core quirk: The converter behind the scenes. Swaps –OH for halogen, and as red phosphorus quietly makes the reagent itself.; Encodes: PCl₅, PCl₃; red P + X₂ → PX₃ in situ; In reactions: PCl₅/PCl₃ replace –OH by –Cl in alcohols and acids (O3, C9). Red P + Br₂ runs HVZ α-halogenation (C9).; Never: Never converts phenol to chlorobenzene in good yield.

characters.section: Carbon's moods and the reactive intermediates
characters.name: Carbon, sp³
characters.text: Character: Carbon, sp³; Core quirk: Relaxed. Spreads four arms evenly in all directions.; Encodes: Tetrahedral, 109°28′, 25% s-character; In reactions: Alkanes and alkyl groups; its C–H is the calmest (pKa ~50).; Never: Never gives up an H to sodium.

characters.section: Carbon's moods and the reactive intermediates
characters.name: Carbon, sp²
characters.text: Character: Carbon, sp²; Core quirk: Alert and flat. Holds three partners in a plane, keeps a loose π pair above and below.; Encodes: Trigonal planar, 120°, 33% s; In reactions: Alkenes, C=O carbon, benzene ring, carbocations.

characters.section: Carbon's moods and the reactive intermediates
characters.name: Carbon, sp
characters.text: Character: Carbon, sp; Core quirk: Strict and straight. Holds electrons tightly, so its H is the most nervous of the hydrocarbon H atoms.; Encodes: Linear, 180°, 50% s; most electronegative carbon; In reactions: Terminal alkyne H leaves to NaNH₂, Na, Ag⁺, Cu⁺ (H7).

characters.section: Carbon's moods and the reactive intermediates
characters.name: Carbocation
characters.text: Character: Carbocation; Core quirk: Insecure and flat. Has lost a partner and its electrons; needs supporters around it. Will rearrange itself (shift an H or CH₃ from next door) to get better support. Open from both faces.; Encodes: 6 electrons, sp², planar; stability 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺; benzylic and allylic extra stable by resonance; 1,2-shifts; In reactions: Forms in HBr addition (H2), SN1 (X2), dehydration (O2), Lucas test (O3), acid hydration (O5). The more alkyl supporters (+I, hyperconjugation), the calmer it is. Attacked from either face, so SN1 at a chiral carbon gives both mirror images (racemisation).; Never: Never keeps its old 3D shape. Never forms easily at a 1° or methyl carbon.

characters.section: Carbon's moods and the reactive intermediates
characters.name: Carbanion
characters.text: Character: Carbanion; Core quirk: Pushy. Has an extra pair of electrons to give away. Prefers fewer alkyl neighbours (they push even more electrons onto it).; Encodes: 8 electrons, pyramidal; stability CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3°; In reactions: Acetylide (H7), the carbon of RMgX (X6, C2), enolate in aldol and haloform (C5, C6). Acts as a nucleophile and a strong base.; Never: Never survives water or any acidic H.

characters.section: Carbon's moods and the reactive intermediates
characters.name: Free radical
characters.text: Character: Free radical; Core quirk: Lonely. One unpaired electron; grabs an H or atom from anyone and leaves a new loner behind, so the story keeps going (chain).; Encodes: 7 electrons; stability 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃•; initiation, propagation, termination; In reactions: Cl• and CH₃• in halogenation (H1); Br• with peroxide (H3); R• coupling in Kolbe electrolysis (H10). The story ends only when two loners meet (termination; CH₃• + CH₃• explains ethane traces).; Never: Never appears without light, heat, peroxide or electrolysis (Kolbe) to start it.

characters.section: Carbon's moods and the reactive intermediates
characters.name: Arenium ion (σ-complex)
characters.text: Character: Arenium ion (σ-complex); Core quirk: The temporarily broken family. Has let a newcomer in and lost its unity for a moment; desperate to restore it.; Encodes: One sp³ carbon; positive charge delocalised; loss of H⁺ restores aromaticity; In reactions: Middle step of every electrophilic substitution (H9): always throws out H⁺ from the carbon that accepted the newcomer.; Never: Never keeps the extra group as an addition product.

characters.section: Carbon's moods and the reactive intermediates
characters.name: Enolate
characters.text: Character: Enolate; Core quirk: Born restless. Forms when a base pulls the α-H off a carbonyl compound; immediately attacks another carbonyl.; Encodes: Resonance-stabilised carbanion; nucleophile; In reactions: Aldol condensation (C5); stepwise replacement of α-H by iodine in the haloform reaction (C6).; Never: Never forms from a compound without α-H (those go to Cannizzaro instead, C7).

characters.name: Hydroxide ion (OH⁻)
characters.text: Character: Hydroxide ion (OH⁻); Core quirk: Two personalities, set by the crowd around it. In water it is an attacker; in alcohol it is a thief of β-hydrogens.; Encodes: Nucleophile when solvated by water; strong base in alcohol; In reactions: Aqueous KOH: attacks carbon (X1, X2). Alcoholic KOH: removes β-H, makes alkenes (X3). Dilute NaOH: removes α-H (aldol, C5). Concentrated NaOH: attacks C=O and triggers hydride transfer (Cannizzaro, C7). With I₂: removes α-H, then attacks C=O (C6).; Never: Never acts as a base for aldol on an aldehyde without α-H.

characters.name: Alkoxide (RO⁻)
characters.text: Character: Alkoxide (RO⁻); Core quirk: Strong and impatient. A powerful attacker, but if the target is crowded it gives up and steals an H instead.; Encodes: Strong nucleophile and strong base; In reactions: Williamson ether synthesis with a 1° halide (O7). With a 3° halide, elimination to an alkene. Formed when sodium meets an alcohol (O1).; Never: Never makes an ether from a 3° alkyl halide.

characters.name: Phenoxide ion
characters.text: Character: Phenoxide ion; Core quirk: Richer and bolder than phenol. Its negative charge floods the ring, so it attacks even weak electrophiles, always at ortho or para.; Encodes: O⁻ is a stronger +R donor than –OH; In reactions: Attacks CO₂ (Kolbe's reaction, P5) and dichlorocarbene (Reimer–Tiemann, P4) at ortho. Couples with diazonium ions at para (alkaline medium, A7). Attacks alkyl halides on oxygen (aryl ethers, O7).; Never: Never attacks with its ring carbon at meta.

characters.name: Cyanide ion (CN⁻)
characters.text: Character: Cyanide ion (CN⁻); Core quirk: Two-faced (ambident). Can attack with carbon or with nitrogen; the partner it arrives with decides. Brings one extra carbon.; Encodes: Ambident nucleophile; KCN ionic, AgCN covalent; In reactions: With K⁺: attacks with C → nitrile (X5). With Ag⁺: only N is free → isocyanide. Adds to C=O (HCN, cyanohydrin, C1). From CuCN replaces N₂ (A6).; Never: Never gives isocyanide from KCN, or nitrile from AgCN.

characters.name: Nitrite ion (NO₂⁻)
characters.text: Character: Nitrite ion (NO₂⁻); Core quirk: Two-faced too. O or N attacks, depending on the partner.; Encodes: Ambident; In reactions: KNO₂ → O attacks → alkyl nitrite R–O–N=O. AgNO₂ → N attacks → nitroalkane R–NO₂ (X5).

characters.name: Hydride ion (H⁻), from LiAlH₄/NaBH₄
characters.text: Character: Hydride ion (H⁻), from LiAlH₄/NaBH₄; Core quirk: The gift-giver. Always delivers a pair of electrons with a hydrogen to an exposed carbon.; Encodes: Nucleophilic H; In reactions: Adds to the carbonyl carbon (C3); see LiAlH₄ and NaBH₄ for who reduces what.; Never: Never adds to an isolated C=C.

characters.name: Proton (H⁺)
characters.text: Character: Proton (H⁺); Core quirk: The desperate first-mover. Owns nothing, wants electrons, always strikes first.; Encodes: Electrophile; acid catalyst; In reactions: First step of HBr addition (H2), acid hydration (O5), dehydration (O2), esterification (O6), ether cleavage (O8).

characters.name: Nitronium ion (NO₂⁺)
characters.text: Character: Nitronium ion (NO₂⁺); Core quirk: Made in the acid mix, born to attack rings.; Encodes: Generated by HNO₃ + 2H₂SO₄; In reactions: Electrophile in nitration (H9).; Never: Never appears without concentrated sulphuric acid in the story.

characters.name: Nitrosonium ion (NO⁺)
characters.text: Character: Nitrosonium ion (NO⁺); Core quirk: The diazotiser. Appears only from cold nitrous acid.; Encodes: From NaNO₂ + HCl; In reactions: Attacked by the nitrogen of a 1° amine (A5).

characters.name: Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂)
characters.text: Character: Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂); Core quirk: Appears only when chloroform meets strong base. Electron-hungry, neutral.; Encodes: Formed from CHCl₃ + OH⁻; In reactions: Turns 1° amines into isocyanides (carbylamine, A3). Attacks phenoxide at ortho, giving –CHO after hydrolysis (P4).; Never: Never reacts with 2° or 3° amines to give isocyanide.

characters.name: Acylium ion (RCO⁺)
characters.text: Character: Acylium ion (RCO⁺); Core quirk: The precise attacker in acylation.; Encodes: Formed from RCOCl + AlCl₃; In reactions: Friedel–Crafts acylation (H9, C8).

characters.name: Diazonium ion (ArN₂⁺)
characters.text: Character: Diazonium ion (ArN₂⁺); Core quirk: Lives only in the cold, with an exit always ready. Its N₂ leaves as gas and anyone can take its seat; as an attacker it is weak and only couples with very rich rings.; Encodes: Stable at 273–278 K (aromatic only); N₂ a perfect leaving group; weak electrophile; In reactions: Replaced by Cl, Br, CN (Cu(I) salts), I (KI), F (HBF₄, heat), H (H₃PO₂ or ethanol), OH (warm water) (A6). Couples at para with phenoxide (alkaline) or aniline (mildly acidic) to give azo dyes (A7).; Never: Never survives warming in water (becomes phenol). Never exists as an aliphatic salt in a story: it decomposes at once.

characters.name: Leaving groups
characters.text: Character: Leaving groups; Core quirk: Their willingness to leave sets the speed of substitution.; Encodes: Stability of the departing anion; C–X strength; In reactions: I⁻ leaves most easily, then Br⁻, Cl⁻; F⁻ barely leaves. –OH leaves only after protonation (as H₂O). N₂ is the best of all. –CI₃ leaves in the haloform reaction (C6).; Never: –OH never leaves unprotonated.

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –OH (phenol)
characters.text: Group on the ring: –OH (phenol); Seating quirk: Warm host. Pulls newcomers into the seats beside and opposite it. So welcoming that in a polar crowd (bromine water) it fills all three seats.; Activity: Strongly activating; Encodes: +R lone pair into ring; In reactions / special behaviour: Bromine water → 2,4,6-tribromophenol; Br₂ in CS₂, cold → one newcomer, o or p (P2). Dilute HNO₃ → o- and p-nitrophenol; conc. HNO₃ → picric acid (P3). The ortho product keeps a private hydrogen bond, so it is steam volatile.; Never: Never sends a newcomer to meta. Never needs a Lewis acid.

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –O⁻ (phenoxide)
characters.text: Group on the ring: –O⁻ (phenoxide); Seating quirk: Warmer host than –OH. Welcomes even weak guests.; Activity: Very strongly activating; Encodes: Full negative charge; In reactions / special behaviour: Kolbe's (CO₂) and Reimer–Tiemann (:CCl₂) at ortho (P4, P5); azo coupling at para (A7).

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –NH₂ (aniline)
characters.text: Group on the ring: –NH₂ (aniline); Seating quirk: The warmest host, but nervous in acid. Fills 2,4,6 with bromine water. In acid it turns into –NH₃⁺, a germophobe.; Activity: Strongly activating; Encodes: +R; basic N; In reactions / special behaviour: Bromine water → 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (A8). Nitration in acid → about 51% para, 47% meta, 2% ortho. Handcuffs AlCl₃, so no Friedel–Crafts. Tamed by acetylation into –NHCOCH₃.; Never: Never does Friedel–Crafts. Never gives a clean mononitro product directly.

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –NHCOCH₃ (acetanilide)
characters.text: Group on the ring: –NHCOCH₃ (acetanilide); Seating quirk: Polite host. Same seats as –NH₂ but calmer: lets in one newcomer, mostly at para.; Activity: Moderately activating; Encodes: N lone pair shared with C=O; In reactions / special behaviour: Used to get p-bromoaniline (bromination, then hydrolysis back to –NH₂) (A8).

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –OCH₃ (anisole)
characters.text: Group on the ring: –OCH₃ (anisole); Seating quirk: Host. o/p.; Activity: Activating; Encodes: +R; In reactions / special behaviour: o/p substitution; with HI it stays on the ring and loses only CH₃ (O8).; Never: Never leaves the ring as I–C₆H₅.

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –CH₃ and other alkyl groups
characters.text: Group on the ring: –CH₃ and other alkyl groups; Seating quirk: Mild host with a weak spot. Sends newcomers o/p, but its own benzylic hydrogens are vulnerable to oxidisers and to chlorine in light.; Activity: Weakly activating; Encodes: +I and hyperconjugation; benzylic C–H; In reactions / special behaviour: Cl₂ + FeCl₃ → ring; Cl₂ in sunlight → side chain (benzyl chloride). KMnO₄ turns it into –COOH (becomes a germophobe). CrO₂Cl₂ turns it into –CHO (Étard, C8).; Never: A tert-butyl group (no benzylic H) is never oxidised by KMnO₄.

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –Cl, –Br, –I (haloarene)
characters.text: Group on the ring: –Cl, –Br, –I (haloarene); Seating quirk: Grumpy but polite. Slows the whole party down, yet still offers the ortho and para seats. Stubborn about leaving the ring itself.; Activity: Deactivating; Encodes: −I outweighs +R for rate; +R decides position; In reactions / special behaviour: o/p products in halogenation, nitration, sulphonation, Friedel–Crafts (X7).; Never: Never sends newcomers to meta. Never leaves the ring easily (needs 623 K, 300 atm, or an –NO₂ at o/p).

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –NO₂
characters.text: Group on the ring: –NO₂; Seating quirk: Strict germophobe. Won't let anyone sit next to it or opposite it: newcomers get only the meta seats. Drains the ring, so electrophiles come slowly. But it helps nucleophiles: a halogen at o/p to it leaves easily.; Activity: Strongly deactivating; Encodes: −R and −I; In reactions / special behaviour: Meta products (Conversions 7, 12). Raises acidity of phenol when at o/p (P1). Makes o/p-nitrohaloarenes easy to substitute (X7). Sn/HCl or Fe/HCl turns it into –NH₂, a warm host (A9).; Never: Never allows Friedel–Crafts on its ring. Never directs o/p.

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –CHO, –COR
characters.text: Group on the ring: –CHO, –COR; Seating quirk: Germophobes. Meta only.; Activity: Deactivating; Encodes: −R, −I; In reactions / special behaviour: Meta substitution on benzaldehyde and acetophenone.; Never: Never direct o/p.

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –COOH
characters.text: Group on the ring: –COOH; Seating quirk: Germophobe that also handcuffs AlCl₃. Meta only.; Activity: Deactivating; Encodes: −R, −I; binds the Lewis acid; In reactions / special behaviour: Nitration → m-nitrobenzoic acid (Conversions 12).; Never: Never undergoes Friedel–Crafts (C9).

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –CN, –SO₃H
characters.text: Group on the ring: –CN, –SO₃H; Seating quirk: Germophobes. –SO₃H is a temporary guest: sulphonation can be reversed.; Activity: Deactivating; Encodes: −R, −I; In reactions / special behaviour: Meta substitution.; Never: Never direct o/p.

characters.section: The benzene ring and the seating rules
characters.name: –NH₃⁺ (anilinium)
characters.text: Group on the ring: –NH₃⁺ (anilinium); Seating quirk: Germophobe: what –NH₂ becomes in strong acid.; Activity: Deactivating; Encodes: Positive charge, no free lone pair; In reactions / special behaviour: Explains the 47% meta product in nitration of aniline (A8).

characters.section: Transformations that change a group's seating quirk
characters.name: –NO₂
characters.text: From: –NO₂; Reagent: Sn/HCl or Fe/HCl; To: –NH₂; Quirk change: Germophobe → warmest host

characters.section: Transformations that change a group's seating quirk
characters.name: –CH₃
characters.text: From: –CH₃; Reagent: KMnO₄, then H⁺; To: –COOH; Quirk change: Mild host → germophobe

characters.section: Transformations that change a group's seating quirk
characters.name: –CH₃
characters.text: From: –CH₃; Reagent: CrO₂Cl₂, then H₃O⁺; To: –CHO; Quirk change: Mild host → germophobe

characters.section: Transformations that change a group's seating quirk
characters.name: –NH₂
characters.text: From: –NH₂; Reagent: Strong acid; To: –NH₃⁺; Quirk change: Warmest host → germophobe

characters.section: Transformations that change a group's seating quirk
characters.name: –NH₂
characters.text: From: –NH₂; Reagent: Acetic anhydride; To: –NHCOCH₃; Quirk change: Loud host → polite host

characters.section: Transformations that change a group's seating quirk
characters.name: –NH₂
characters.text: From: –NH₂; Reagent: NaNO₂/HCl (cold), then H₃PO₂; To: –H; Quirk change: Host leaves after directing (temporary director)

characters.section: Transformations that change a group's seating quirk
characters.name: –NH₂
characters.text: From: –NH₂; Reagent: NaNO₂/HCl (cold), then CuX, KI, H₂O; To: –X, –CN, –I, –OH; Quirk change: Host becomes whatever replaces N₂

characters.name: Alkane
characters.text: Character: Alkane; Core quirk: Lazy. Ignores almost everyone; wakes up only for radicals with light or heat.; Encodes: Strong, non-polar C–C and C–H bonds; In reactions: Radical halogenation (H1). Made by Wurtz, decarboxylation, Kolbe, hydrogenation (H10).; Never: Never reacts with Br₂ water, KMnO₄, Na or acids under normal conditions.

characters.name: Alkene (C=C)
characters.text: Character: Alkene (C=C); Core quirk: Generous with its loose π pair. Reaches out to any electrophile; always follows the crowd rule: H goes where H's already are.; Encodes: π electrons; Markovnikov; In reactions: Electrophilic additions: HX (H2), Br₂ (H4), H₂O/H⁺ (O5). Reverses only for HBr + peroxide (H3) or with B₂H₆ (O5). Cold Baeyer's reagent makes a diol; hot KMnO₄ and ozone split it in two (H8). Its tells: decolourises Br₂/CCl₄ and pink KMnO₄.; Never: Never gives anti-Markovnikov HCl or HI addition.

characters.name: Terminal alkyne (≡C–H)
characters.text: Character: Terminal alkyne (≡C–H); Core quirk: Has a nervous hydrogen. Gives it up to strong bases and to silver or copper ions.; Encodes: sp C–H acidic (pKa ~25); In reactions: NaNH₂/Na → acetylide (H7); ammoniacal AgNO₃ → white ppt, ammoniacal Cu₂Cl₂ → red ppt. Hydration: ethyne → acetaldehyde, others → ketones (H5). Lindlar → cis-alkene; Na/liq. NH₃ → trans-alkene (H6). Three ethynes in a red-hot iron tube → benzene.; Never: Never gives an acetylide if internal (no ≡C–H).

characters.name: 1° haloalkane
characters.text: Character: 1° haloalkane; Core quirk: Open to a backside attack. Uncrowded, so attackers come from behind.; Encodes: SN2 favoured; In reactions: Substitution (X1), Williamson partner (O7), Gabriel partner (A2).; Never: Never goes by SN1 (1° carbocation too unstable).

characters.name: 3° haloalkane
characters.text: Character: 3° haloalkane; Core quirk: Crowded and self-leaving. Halogen walks out on its own (SN1); with a strong base the molecule eliminates.; Encodes: SN1 and elimination favoured; In reactions: SN1 in water (X2); alc. KOH → alkene (X3); alkoxide → alkene instead of ether (O7).; Never: Never undergoes SN2.

characters.name: Allylic and benzylic halides
characters.text: Character: Allylic and benzylic halides; Core quirk: Fast leavers. Their carbocation is supported by resonance.; Encodes: Resonance-stabilised carbocation; In reactions: Very fast SN1.

characters.name: Haloarene
characters.text: Character: Haloarene; Core quirk: Stubborn. Its halogen is half-married to the ring.; Encodes: C–X partial double-bond character; sp² C; In reactions: Leaves only at 623 K, 300 atm (Dow), or easily when –NO₂ sits at o/p (X7). Wurtz–Fittig, Fittig with Na.; Never: Never undergoes ordinary SN1/SN2. Never used as the electrophile in Gabriel or Williamson.

characters.name: 1° alcohol
characters.text: Character: 1° alcohol; Core quirk: Patient. Slow in the Lucas test; oxidises in two stages.; Encodes: Unstable 1° carbocation; two H on carbinol carbon; In reactions: Lucas: no turbidity at room temperature (O3). PCC → aldehyde; K₂Cr₂O₇/KMnO₄ → acid; Cu 573 K → aldehyde (O4). Most acidic alcohol class (O1).; Never: Never turbid in Lucas at room temperature.

characters.name: 2° alcohol
characters.text: Character: 2° alcohol; Core quirk: In between.; Encodes: One H on carbinol carbon; In reactions: Lucas: turbid within about 5 minutes. Oxidised to a ketone; Cu 573 K → ketone.; Never: Never oxidised to a carboxylic acid with the same carbons.

characters.name: 3° alcohol
characters.text: Character: 3° alcohol; Core quirk: Quick to lose its –OH, refuses oxidation.; Encodes: Stable 3° carbocation; no H on carbinol carbon; In reactions: Lucas: turbid at once. Easiest to dehydrate (O2). Cu 573 K → alkene, not a carbonyl.; Never: Never oxidised by K₂Cr₂O₇.

characters.name: Phenol
characters.text: Character: Phenol; Core quirk: Acid with limits. Stronger than alcohols, too weak for bicarbonate; its oxygen never lets go of the ring.; Encodes: Phenoxide resonance; strong C–O; In reactions: Reacts with NaOH, not NaHCO₃ (P1). Violet with neutral FeCl₃. Zn dust → benzene. Warm host for substitution (see seating rules).; Never: Never gives chlorobenzene with HCl. Never fizzes with NaHCO₃.

characters.name: Ether
characters.text: Character: Ether; Core quirk: Quiet and unreactive, cracked only by HI.; Encodes: No O–H; C–O–C stable; In reactions: HI: I⁻ attacks the smaller alkyl group (SN2); a 3° group leaves by SN1. Aryl–O stays intact (O8).; Never: Never releases H₂ with Na.

characters.name: Aldehyde
characters.text: Character: Aldehyde; Core quirk: Approachable and easy to oxidise. One alkyl guard, and a C–H on the carbonyl carbon that any oxidiser can take.; Encodes: Less steric/+I than ketones; oxidisable C–H; In reactions: Nucleophilic addition (C1). Tollens' positive (all aldehydes); Fehling's positive (aliphatic only) (C4). With α-H: aldol (C5). Without α-H: Cannizzaro (C7).; Never: Aromatic aldehydes never pass Fehling's.

characters.name: Formaldehyde (HCHO)
characters.text: Character: Formaldehyde (HCHO); Core quirk: The most reactive carbonyl, and always the one sacrificed.; Encodes: No alkyl group; no α-H; In reactions: Most reactive in addition (C1). Grignard + HCHO → 1° alcohol (C2). In crossed Cannizzaro HCHO is always oxidised to formate (C7).; Never: Never gives iodoform. Never undergoes aldol as the enolate partner.

characters.name: Ketone
characters.text: Character: Ketone; Core quirk: Guarded by two alkyl groups. Harder to approach; refuses mild oxidisers.; Encodes: Steric and +I hindrance; no carbonyl C–H; In reactions: Addition slower than aldehydes. Grignard → 3° alcohol. CH₃CO– ketones give iodoform (C6). Clemmensen/Wolff–Kishner → CH₂.; Never: Never passes Tollens' or Fehling's.

characters.name: Carboxylic acid
characters.text: Character: Carboxylic acid; Core quirk: The proudest acid. Its C=O is busy in resonance, so it ignores the carbonyl tests. Fizzes with bicarbonate.; Encodes: Resonance-stabilised carboxylate; In reactions: NaHCO₃ → CO₂ (C9). SOCl₂/PCl₅ → acid chloride. Esterification: loses its –OH (O6). HVZ at α-carbon. Decarboxylation with sodalime (−1 C). LiAlH₄/B₂H₆ → 1° alcohol. Acidity rises with −I groups.; Never: Never reduced by NaBH₄. Never gives 2,4-DNP or Tollens'.

characters.name: Acid chloride
characters.text: Character: Acid chloride; Core quirk: Eager to swap its Cl.; Encodes: Good leaving group next to C=O; In reactions: NH₃ → amide; H₂/Pd–BaSO₄ → aldehyde (C8); acylating agent (Friedel–Crafts, acetylation of aniline).

characters.name: Amide
characters.text: Character: Amide; Core quirk: Its nitrogen is spoken for. Lone pair shared with C=O, so nearly neutral; N–H slightly acidic.; Encodes: Resonance with C=O; In reactions: Br₂/NaOH → amine with one carbon fewer (A1). LiAlH₄ → amine with the same carbons (A9). P₂O₅ → nitrile.; Never: Never basic like an amine.

characters.name: Nitrile
characters.text: Character: Nitrile; Core quirk: The universal converter.; Encodes: C≡N can be hydrolysed, reduced or attacked; In reactions: H₃O⁺ → acid; LiAlH₄ or H₂/Ni → 1° amine; SnCl₂/HCl → aldehyde (Stephen); RMgX → ketone (C2, C8).

characters.name: 1° amine
characters.text: Character: 1° amine; Core quirk: Two hydrogens on nitrogen decide its tests.; Encodes: Two N–H; In reactions: Carbylamine positive (A3). Hinsberg product dissolves in alkali (A4). HNO₂: aliphatic → alcohol + N₂; aromatic (cold) → diazonium (A5).; Never: 2° and 3° amines never give carbylamine.

characters.name: 2° amine
characters.text: Character: 2° amine; Core quirk: One N–H.; Encodes: One N–H; In reactions: Hinsberg product insoluble in alkali. Most basic in water among methyl and ethyl amines.

characters.name: 3° amine
characters.text: Character: 3° amine; Core quirk: No N–H.; Encodes: No N–H; In reactions: No Hinsberg reaction. Lower boiling point than 1°/2° (no H-bonding).; Never: Never reacts with Hinsberg's reagent.

characters.name: Aniline
characters.text: Character: Aniline; Core quirk: A host on the ring, a weak base off it.; Encodes: Lone pair delocalised into ring; In reactions: Weaker base than NH₃ and alkylamines. See –NH₂ in seating rules.; Never: Never does Friedel–Crafts.

characters.name: Grignard reagent (RMgX)
characters.text: Character: Grignard reagent (RMgX); Core quirk: Aggressive but terrified of water. Its carbon is pushy (carbanion-like); any acidic H destroys it.; Encodes: C–Mg polar, C δ−; In reactions: HCHO → 1°, RCHO → 2°, ketone → 3° alcohol; CO₂ → acid; nitrile → ketone (C2). Water, alcohol, amine, terminal alkyne → alkane (X6).; Never: Never made or used outside dry ether.

characters.name: Sodium
characters.text: Character: Sodium; Core quirk: Hothead and giver. Gives away its one electron instantly; explodes into action on contact with water, releasing flammable hydrogen. Kept locked in kerosene.; Encodes: Low ionisation energy; violently exothermic with water; In reactions: Releases H₂ from acidic H: alcohols (O1), terminal alkynes (H7). Joins two alkyl groups (Wurtz, Fittig, H10, X7). In liquid NH₃ makes trans-alkenes (H6). Sodium fusion turns N, S, X into ions for testing.; Never: Never kept in water or air. Never releases H₂ from alkanes or alkenes.

characters.name: Potassium
characters.text: Character: Potassium; Core quirk: Bigger hothead than sodium.; Encodes: Even lower ionisation energy; In reactions: Same as sodium, more violent. Mostly appears as K⁺ partner: decides whether OH⁻ attacks or steals (aq. vs alc. KOH, X3), whether CN⁻ and NO₂⁻ attack with C/O (X5).

characters.name: Magnesium
characters.text: Character: Magnesium; Core quirk: Makes carbon pushy. Slips between carbon and halogen, turning the carbon into an attacker.; Encodes: Mg less electronegative than C; In reactions: Forms RMgX in dry ether (X6).; Never: Never works in wet solvent.

characters.name: Lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH₄)
characters.text: Character: Lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH₄); Core quirk: The generous reducer. Gives hydride to almost any C=O or C≡N.; Encodes: Strong hydride donor; In reactions: Aldehydes, ketones, acids, esters → alcohols; amides, nitriles → amines (C3, A9).; Never: Never reduces an isolated C=C.

characters.name: Sodium borohydride (NaBH₄)
characters.text: Character: Sodium borohydride (NaBH₄); Core quirk: The selective reducer. Only aldehydes and ketones.; Encodes: Milder hydride donor; In reactions: Aldehyde → 1° alcohol; ketone → 2° alcohol (C3).; Never: Never reduces acids or esters.

characters.name: Diborane (B₂H₆)
characters.text: Character: Diborane (B₂H₆); Core quirk: Electron-hungry but polite. Sits on the less crowded carbon of a double bond and leaves the crowded one to hydrogen.; Encodes: Electron-deficient boron; In reactions: Hydroboration–oxidation → anti-Markovnikov alcohol (O5). Reduces acids to 1° alcohols.; Never: Never gives the Markovnikov alcohol.

characters.name: Aluminium chloride (anhydrous AlCl₃)
characters.text: Character: Aluminium chloride (anhydrous AlCl₃); Core quirk: The matchmaker. Creates the attacker (R⁺, RCO⁺, Cl⁺) and walks away unchanged. Refuses rings that are too poor or that handcuff it.; Encodes: Lewis acid, regenerated; In reactions: Friedel–Crafts alkylation and acylation; chlorination of benzene (H9); Gattermann–Koch (C8).; Never: Never works on nitrobenzene, benzoic acid or aniline. Never works wet.

characters.name: Ferric chloride / bromide (FeCl₃, FeBr₃)
characters.text: Character: Ferric chloride / bromide (FeCl₃, FeBr₃); Core quirk: Junior matchmaker for halogenation. As a test reagent, turns phenols violet.; Encodes: Lewis acid; complex with phenols; In reactions: Halogenation of benzene (H9). Neutral FeCl₃ test for phenol (P6).

characters.name: Zinc
characters.text: Character: Zinc; Core quirk: The quiet cleaner. Removes oxygen or unwanted oxidiser without fuss.; Encodes: Reducing metal; In reactions: Zn–Hg/HCl: C=O → CH₂ (Clemmensen, C3). Zn/H₂O destroys H₂O₂ after ozonolysis (H8). Zn dust strips O from phenol → benzene. ZnCl₂ helps –OH leave in the Lucas test (O3).

characters.name: Tin (Sn/HCl, SnCl₂)
characters.text: Character: Tin (Sn/HCl, SnCl₂); Core quirk: The acid-loving reducer.; Encodes: Reducing metal in acid; In reactions: Sn/HCl: –NO₂ → –NH₂ (A9). SnCl₂/HCl: nitrile → aldehyde (Stephen, C8).

characters.name: Iron (Fe/HCl)
characters.text: Character: Iron (Fe/HCl); Core quirk: The frugal reducer. Needs little acid because it regenerates its own HCl.; Encodes: FeCl₂ hydrolyses, releasing HCl; In reactions: –NO₂ → –NH₂ (preferred method, A9). Red-hot iron tube (873 K) turns three ethynes into benzene.

characters.name: Copper
characters.text: Character: Copper; Core quirk: The fixer. As metal at 573 K, strips hydrogen from alcohols; as Cu(I), replaces the diazonium's N₂; as Cu²⁺ in Fehling's, a fussy judge of aldehydes.; Encodes: Dehydrogenation catalyst; Cu(I) mediates replacement; Cu²⁺ mild oxidant; In reactions: Cu 573 K: 1° → aldehyde, 2° → ketone, 3° → alkene (O4). CuCl, CuBr, CuCN (Sandmeyer); Cu powder (Gattermann) (A6). Fehling's: red Cu₂O with aliphatic aldehydes (C4). Ammoniacal Cu₂Cl₂: red precipitate with terminal alkynes.; Never: Fehling's never passes benzaldehyde or ketones.

characters.name: Silver
characters.text: Character: Silver; Core quirk: The generous judge (Tollens') and the covalent clinger (AgCN, AgNO₂).; Encodes: Ag⁺ mild oxidant; Ag–C/Ag–N bonds largely covalent; In reactions: Tollens': silver mirror with every aldehyde, aromatic too (C4). AgCN → isocyanide, AgNO₂ → nitroalkane (X5). AgF → alkyl fluoride (X4). AgNO₃ tests halide ions (white, pale yellow, yellow). Ammoniacal AgNO₃: white precipitate with terminal alkynes.; Never: Tollens' never passes ketones. Alkyl halides never give a direct AgNO₃ precipitate.

characters.name: Mercury (Hg²⁺)
characters.text: Character: Mercury (Hg²⁺); Core quirk: The hydration sponsor. Without it, water and an alkyne ignore each other.; Encodes: Hg²⁺ catalyses alkyne hydration; In reactions: Alkyne + H₂O → aldehyde (ethyne only) or ketone (H5). Zn–Hg amalgam in Clemmensen. Hg₂F₂ in Swarts.

characters.name: Platinum, palladium
characters.text: Character: Platinum, palladium; Core quirk: Effortless hydrogenators. Work at room temperature.; Encodes: Finely divided metal catalysts; In reactions: Alkenes, alkynes → alkanes (H6).

characters.name: Nickel
characters.text: Character: Nickel; Core quirk: Hydrogenator that needs heat (523–573 K).; Encodes: Catalyst; In reactions: Alkenes, alkynes → alkanes; nitriles → amines; C=O → alcohols.

characters.name: Poisoned palladium (Lindlar; Pd/BaSO₄)
characters.text: Character: Poisoned palladium (Lindlar; Pd/BaSO₄); Core quirk: Tired on purpose. Stops halfway.; Encodes: Catalyst deactivated by S compounds, quinoline or BaSO₄; In reactions: Lindlar: alkyne → cis-alkene (H6). Pd/BaSO₄: acid chloride → aldehyde (Rosenmund, C8).; Never: Never reduces all the way to alkane or alcohol.

characters.name: Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄)
characters.text: Character: Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄); Core quirk: Two tempers. Cold, dilute and alkaline, it is gentle: adds two –OH across a double bond and its pink fades. Hot, it is a destroyer: splits C=C and chops any side chain with a benzylic H down to –COOH.; Encodes: Mn(VII), strong oxidant; In reactions: Baeyer's test (main tab, Mn). Hot: alkene → acids/ketones/CO₂; toluene, ethylbenzene, propylbenzene → benzoic acid. 1° alcohols, aldehydes → acids (O4).; Never: Never oxidises tert-butylbenzene. Never stops at an aldehyde.

characters.name: Potassium dichromate (acidified)
characters.text: Character: Potassium dichromate (acidified); Core quirk: The strict examiner. Oxidises 1° and 2° alcohols, refuses 3°; turns from orange to green when it works.; Encodes: Cr(VI) → Cr(III); needs an H on the carbinol carbon; In reactions: 1° → aldehyde → acid; 2° → ketone (O4).; Never: Never oxidises a 3° alcohol.

characters.name: PCC
characters.text: Character: PCC; Core quirk: The gentle examiner. Stops at the aldehyde.; Encodes: Mild Cr(VI) reagent; In reactions: 1° alcohol → aldehyde (O4).; Never: Never makes a carboxylic acid.

characters.name: Chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂)
characters.text: Character: Chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂); Core quirk: The precision tool. Turns a ring's –CH₃ into –CHO and nothing more.; Encodes: Étard reaction; In reactions: Toluene → benzaldehyde (C8).; Never: Never goes on to benzoic acid.

characters.name: Ozone (O₃)
characters.text: Character: Ozone (O₃); Core quirk: The cutter. Splits a double bond into two carbonyls, with Zn standing guard.; Encodes: Ozonide, then Zn/H₂O; In reactions: Locates C=C (H8).

characters.name: Concentrated sulphuric acid
characters.text: Character: Concentrated sulphuric acid; Core quirk: Temperature decides its mood. A dehydrator, a catalyst and the maker of NO₂⁺.; Encodes: Dehydrating agent; strong acid; In reactions: Ethanol at 443 K → ethene; at 413 K → diethyl ether (O2). Catalyses esterification (O6). With HNO₃ makes NO₂⁺ (H9). Fuming: sulphonation.

characters.name: Nitric acid
characters.text: Character: Nitric acid; Core quirk: Dilute, it is polite; concentrated with H₂SO₄, it is fierce.; Encodes: Concentration sets the electrophile; In reactions: Dilute, 298 K: phenol → o- and p-nitrophenol. Conc.: phenol → picric acid (P3). Conc. + H₂SO₄: nitration of benzene (H9). Oxidising helper for iodination.

characters.name: Hydrogen halides (HX)
characters.text: Character: Hydrogen halides (HX); Core quirk: Rank by strength: HI > HBr > HCl.; Encodes: H–X bond strength and acidity; In reactions: Add to alkenes (H2); convert alcohols to halides (O3, ZnCl₂ needed for HCl). HI cracks ethers (O8). HBr alone has the peroxide switch (H3).; Never: HCl and HI never add anti-Markovnikov.

characters.name: Sodium hydroxide
characters.text: Character: Sodium hydroxide; Core quirk: Strength decides its role. Dilute: an α-H thief (aldol). Concentrated: an attacker that starts a hydride hand-off (Cannizzaro).; Encodes: Base vs nucleophile; In reactions: Aldol (C5), Cannizzaro (C7), haloform with I₂ (C6), Hofmann with Br₂ (A1), Reimer–Tiemann with CHCl₃ (P4). Turns phenol into phenoxide (P1). Sodalime (with CaO) decarboxylates (H10).

characters.name: Sodamide (NaNH₂)
characters.text: Character: Sodamide (NaNH₂); Core quirk: Strong base for stubborn hydrogens.; Encodes: Stronger base than acetylide; In reactions: Terminal alkyne → acetylide (H7); second elimination to an alkyne.

characters.name: Sodium bicarbonate
characters.text: Character: Sodium bicarbonate; Core quirk: The acid detector. Fizzes only with acids stronger than carbonic acid.; Encodes: Weak base; In reactions: Carboxylic acids → CO₂ effervescence (C9).; Never: Never fizzes with phenol or alcohols.

characters.name: Bromine water
characters.text: Character: Bromine water; Core quirk: Floods a rich ring. Polar water makes Br₂ aggressive.; Encodes: Polar solvent polarises Br₂; In reactions: Phenol → 2,4,6-tribromophenol; aniline → 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (P2, A8).; Never: Never stops at one bromine on phenol or aniline.

characters.name: Br₂ in CS₂ (cold)
characters.text: Character: Br₂ in CS₂ (cold); Core quirk: Calm bromine. Non-polar solvent, one newcomer only.; Encodes: Weakly polarised Br₂; In reactions: Phenol → o- and p-bromophenol (P2).

characters.name: Br₂ in CCl₄
characters.text: Character: Br₂ in CCl₄; Core quirk: The unsaturation detective. Red-brown colour vanishes on meeting C=C or C≡C.; Encodes: Electrophilic addition; In reactions: Test for unsaturation (H4).; Never: Never decolourises with an alkane or benzene.

characters.name: Iodine + NaOH
characters.text: Character: Iodine + NaOH; Core quirk: The CH₃CO– detector.; Encodes: Haloform reaction; In reactions: Yellow CHI₃ from CH₃CO– and CH₃CH(OH)– compounds (C6).; Never: Never positive with methanol, HCHO, propan-1-ol or pentan-3-one.

characters.name: Thionyl chloride, PCl₅, PCl₃
characters.text: Character: Thionyl chloride, PCl₅, PCl₃; Core quirk: Swap –OH for –Cl. SOCl₂ leaves no mess.; Encodes: Chlorinating agents; In reactions: Alcohols → alkyl chlorides (O3); acids → acid chlorides (C9).

characters.name: NaI in dry acetone
characters.text: Character: NaI in dry acetone; Core quirk: The swapper. Trades I for Cl or Br, pushed by its precipitating partner.; Encodes: NaCl/NaBr insoluble in acetone; In reactions: Finkelstein (X4).; Never: Never works in water (the salts would dissolve).

characters.name: Chloroform (CHCl₃)
characters.text: Character: Chloroform (CHCl₃); Core quirk: Hides a carbene, released only by strong base. Turns to poisonous phosgene in light and air.; Encodes: :CCl₂ source; oxidation to COCl₂; In reactions: Carbylamine (A3), Reimer–Tiemann (P4). Stored dark and full (X8).

characters.name: Peroxide
characters.text: Character: Peroxide; Core quirk: The radical starter. Changes only one story: HBr addition.; Encodes: Weak O–O bond; In reactions: Anti-Markovnikov HBr addition (H3).; Never: Never changes HCl or HI addition.

characters.name: HCN
characters.text: Character: HCN; Core quirk: Adds one carbon to a carbonyl, needs a little base to get going.; Encodes: CN⁻ nucleophile; In reactions: Cyanohydrins (C1).

characters.name: NaHSO₃
characters.text: Character: NaHSO₃; Core quirk: The purifier. Forms crystals with aldehydes and some ketones.; Encodes: Addition product; In reactions: C1.

characters.name: NH₂OH, NH₂NH₂, 2,4-DNP
characters.text: Character: NH₂OH, NH₂NH₂, 2,4-DNP; Core quirk: Add, then drop water. 2,4-DNP gives an orange-red solid: the carbonyl detector.; Encodes: Addition–elimination; In reactions: Oximes, hydrazones, 2,4-DNP derivatives (C1). NH₂NH₂ + KOH → Wolff–Kishner (C3).; Never: Never react with carboxylic acids as carbonyls.

characters.name: Nitrous acid (NaNO₂ + HCl)
characters.text: Character: Nitrous acid (NaNO₂ + HCl); Core quirk: The amine sorter. Must be cold.; Encodes: Gives NO⁺; In reactions: 1° aliphatic amine → alcohol + N₂; aniline at 273–278 K → diazonium (A5).

characters.name: Hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂)
characters.text: Character: Hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂); Core quirk: The eraser. Replaces –N₂⁺ with H.; Encodes: Reducing agent; In reactions: Deamination (A6; Conversions 9).

characters.name: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent)
characters.text: Character: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent); Core quirk: Sorts amines by how many N–H they have.; Encodes: Sulphonamide formation; In reactions: 1° soluble in alkali, 2° insoluble, 3° no reaction (A4).

characters.name: Phthalimide + KOH
characters.text: Character: Phthalimide + KOH; Core quirk: Lets exactly one alkyl group in.; Encodes: Acidic N–H, SN2, no over-alkylation; In reactions: Gabriel synthesis of 1° aliphatic amines (A2).; Never: Never makes aromatic amines.

characters.name: Ammonia
characters.text: Character: Ammonia; Core quirk: An indiscriminate attacker on alkyl halides.; Encodes: Repeated alkylation; In reactions: Mixture of 1°, 2°, 3° amines and quaternary salt (A9). With acid chlorides → amides.; Never: Never gives a single clean amine from RX.

characters.name: Carbon dioxide
characters.text: Character: Carbon dioxide; Core quirk: A weak electrophile that only very strong attackers can catch.; Encodes: C between two O; In reactions: Grignard → acid (C2); phenoxide → salicylic acid (P5).; Never: Never reacts with phenol itself in Kolbe's reaction (needs phenoxide).

characters.name: Water and alcohols (polar protic)
characters.text: Character: Water and alcohols (polar protic); Core quirk: The comforting crowd. Surrounds anyone charged and keeps them calm.; Encodes: Solvates ions by hydrogen bonding; Effect on others: Lets halides walk out alone (SN1, X2). Keeps OH⁻ busy, so it attacks instead of stealing H (aq. KOH). Polarises Br₂ (bromine water floods phenol).

characters.name: Alcohol as solvent for KOH
characters.text: Character: Alcohol as solvent for KOH; Core quirk: Leaves the base unguarded.; Encodes: Poor solvation of OH⁻/RO⁻; Effect on others: OH⁻ turns into an H-thief: elimination (X3).

characters.name: Acetone (polar aprotic)
characters.text: Character: Acetone (polar aprotic); Core quirk: Doesn't hug anions. Attackers stay free and strong. Some salts can't stay dissolved here.; Encodes: No O–H; Effect on others: SN2 favoured (X1). NaCl/NaBr precipitate in Finkelstein (X4).

characters.name: Dry ether
characters.text: Character: Dry ether; Core quirk: Strict no-water zone.; Encodes: Aprotic, no acidic H; Effect on others: Required for Grignard (X6) and Wurtz (H10).; Never: Never contains water in a working story.

characters.name: CCl₄, CS₂, CHCl₃ (non-polar)
characters.text: Character: CCl₄, CS₂, CHCl₃ (non-polar); Core quirk: The calm room.; Encodes: Non-polar; Effect on others: Br₂ in CCl₄: clean addition test (H4). Br₂ in CS₂: one bromine on phenol (P2). CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂ (Étard).

characters.name: Kerosene
characters.text: Character: Kerosene; Core quirk: The safe house for hotheads.; Encodes: Unreactive towards Na and K; Effect on others: Stores sodium and potassium away from air and water.

characters.name: Light (hν) and heat
characters.text: Character: Light (hν) and heat; Core quirk: The wake-up call for loners.; Encodes: Homolytic bond breaking; Effect on others: Starts radical chains (H1); side-chain chlorination of toluene.

characters.name: Cold, 273–278 K
characters.text: Character: Cold, 273–278 K; Core quirk: The only weather a diazonium salt survives.; Encodes: Thermal instability of ArN₂⁺; Effect on others: Diazotisation (A5).

characters.name: 443 K vs 413 K (with conc. H₂SO₄)
characters.text: Character: 443 K vs 413 K (with conc. H₂SO₄); Core quirk: Two temperatures, two endings for ethanol.; Encodes: Elimination vs substitution; Effect on others: 443 K → ethene; 413 K → diethyl ether (O2).

characters.name: 573 K with Cu
characters.text: Character: 573 K with Cu; Core quirk: Dehydrogenation heat.; Effect on others: 1°/2° alcohols lose H₂; 3° loses H₂O (O4).

characters.name: 623 K, 300 atm
characters.text: Character: 623 K, 300 atm; Core quirk: The force needed to pull Cl off chlorobenzene.; Encodes: Partial double-bond C–Cl; Effect on others: Dow process (X7).

characters.name: 873 K red-hot iron tube
characters.text: Character: 873 K red-hot iron tube; Core quirk: Where three ethynes become one benzene.; Encodes: Cyclic polymerisation; Effect on others: Ethyne → benzene.

characters.name: Benzene Haveli
characters.text: Character: Benzene Haveli; Filmy quirk: A joint family of six carbon brothers in a circle who share everything, even their electrons. Never splits up.; Real chemistry: Ring of 6 carbons sharing 6 electrons (aromatic). Very stable, so it does substitution, not addition.

characters.name: Daadi
characters.text: Character: Daadi; Filmy quirk: Head of the haveli. Her rule: "Ghar kabhi nahi tootega. Koi naya aayega, toh kisi naukar ki jagah lega." Narrates the lesson at the end of every ring story.; Real chemistry: The aromatic ring is always restored at the end of a substitution.

characters.name: Ramu Kaka (each hydrogen on the ring)
characters.text: Character: Ramu Kaka (each hydrogen on the ring); Filmy quirk: The loyal servant behind each brother. When a guest arrives, he quietly gives up his place and leaves: "Main chalta hoon, malik."; Real chemistry: Each ring carbon has one H. In substitution, the new group takes its place and the H leaves as H⁺.

characters.name: The one-second chaos
characters.text: Character: The one-second chaos; Filmy quirk: When a guest walks in, one brother is holding hands with both the guest and his Ramu Kaka. Everyone panics, until Ramu Kaka leaves.; Real chemistry: The arenium ion: a short-lived stage where one ring carbon holds both the new group and H.

characters.name: When the haveli is forced
characters.text: Character: When the haveli is forced; Filmy quirk: Only a powerful outsider can make the family break its circle: hydrogen with Nickel and heat, or Chlorine under UV light. Daadi never forgives it.; Real chemistry: Benzene adds H₂ (Ni, heat → cyclohexane) or Cl₂ (UV light → hexachlorocyclohexane) only under harsh conditions.

characters.section: Hosts (send the next guest to ortho or para)
characters.name: Methyl, the friendly padosi uncle (–CH₃)
characters.text: Character: Methyl, the friendly padosi uncle (–CH₃); Filmy quirk: "Aao aao, yahin baitho!" Calls guests next to him or opposite. Always has three chamche (hangers-on) standing right beside the haveli: his weak spot.; Real chemistry: –CH₃ is ortho/para directing and mildly activating. Its three H atoms are next to the ring (benzylic H) and can be oxidised.

characters.section: Hosts (send the next guest to ortho or para)
characters.name: Mummy ji, the feeder (–OH, phenol)
characters.text: Character: Mummy ji, the feeder (–OH, phenol); Filmy quirk: Can't stop feeding guests. In a busy kitchen (bromine water) she fills all three seats at once. In a quiet kitchen (Br₂ in CS₂, cold) she serves just one guest.; Real chemistry: –OH strongly activates: bromine water gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol; Br₂ in CS₂ gives o- or p-bromophenol.

characters.section: Hosts (send the next guest to ortho or para)
characters.name: Mummy ji in full mood (–O⁻, phenoxide)
characters.text: Character: Mummy ji in full mood (–O⁻, phenoxide); Filmy quirk: Even warmer: will invite the shyest guests (CO₂, the chloroform carbene) to sit right next to her.; Real chemistry: Phenoxide reacts even with weak electrophiles at ortho: Kolbe's reaction and Reimer–Tiemann.

characters.section: Hosts (send the next guest to ortho or para)
characters.name: Bunty Uncle, the loudest guest at every party (–NH₂, aniline)
characters.text: Character: Bunty Uncle, the loudest guest at every party (–NH₂, aniline); Filmy quirk: The loudest host: fills all three seats with bromine water. Two weaknesses: he grabs bhaiya's hand and won't let go, so no rishta happens (no Friedel–Crafts); and in a sour (acid) room he turns into a germophobe.; Real chemistry: –NH₂ strongly activates (2,4,6-tribromoaniline). Its lone pair binds AlCl₃. In acid it becomes –NH₃⁺, which sends guests to meta (47% meta in nitration).

characters.section: Hosts (send the next guest to ortho or para)
characters.name: Bunty Uncle after marriage (–NHCOCH₃, acetanilide)
characters.text: Character: Bunty Uncle after marriage (–NHCOCH₃, acetanilide); Filmy quirk: Same host, but calmer now. Lets in one guest, usually opposite him.; Real chemistry: Acetylation tames –NH₂: mono-substitution, mostly para.

characters.section: Hosts (send the next guest to ortho or para)
characters.name: Mausa ji with the dhoti (–OCH₃, anisole)
characters.text: Character: Mausa ji with the dhoti (–OCH₃, anisole); Filmy quirk: A host like Mummy ji. Even HI can only take away his topi (the CH₃), never pull him off the haveli.; Real chemistry: –OCH₃ is o/p directing. Anisole + HI → phenol + CH₃I, never iodobenzene.

characters.section: Hosts (send the next guest to ortho or para)
characters.name: Grumpy Chacha (–Cl, –Br, –I on the ring)
characters.text: Character: Grumpy Chacha (–Cl, –Br, –I on the ring); Filmy quirk: Complains, slows the whole party down, but still politely points guests to the seats next to him or opposite. Very hard to throw out of the haveli.; Real chemistry: Halogens deactivate the ring but direct ortho/para. A haloarene loses its halogen only at 623 K and 300 atm, or with –NO₂ at o/p.

characters.section: Germophobes (allow only one seat away: meta)
characters.name: Bade Sahab, the germophobe NRI uncle (–COOH)
characters.text: Character: Bade Sahab, the germophobe NRI uncle (–COOH); Filmy quirk: Back from abroad, sanitiser in pocket: "Doori banaye rakhein! Ek seat chhod ke baitho!" Makes the whole haveli cold. Never lets bhaiya arrange a rishta in his house.; Real chemistry: –COOH is meta directing and deactivating. Benzoic acid does not undergo Friedel–Crafts.

characters.section: Germophobes (allow only one seat away: meta)
characters.name: The hostel warden (–NO₂)
characters.text: Character: The hostel warden (–NO₂); Filmy quirk: The strictest germophobe. Meta seats only; the house becomes so cold that bhaiya never comes again. But he secretly helps one kind of person: if Grumpy Chacha sits next to or opposite him, he helps Chacha get out.; Real chemistry: –NO₂: strongly deactivating, meta directing; no Friedel–Crafts. It makes a halogen at o/p easy to replace by OH⁻.

characters.section: Germophobes (allow only one seat away: meta)
characters.name: The snobbish cousins (–CHO, –COR, –CN)
characters.text: Character: The snobbish cousins (–CHO, –COR, –CN); Filmy quirk: Same germophobe rule: meta only.; Real chemistry: Deactivating, meta directing.

characters.section: Germophobes (allow only one seat away: meta)
characters.name: The paying guest (–SO₃H)
characters.text: Character: The paying guest (–SO₃H); Filmy quirk: Germophobe who can be asked to vacate.; Real chemistry: –SO₃H is meta directing; sulphonation is reversible.

characters.name: Padosi uncle → Bade Sahab
characters.text: Makeover: Padosi uncle → Bade Sahab; What happens in the story: The purple saas throws out his three chamche; he returns in a suit as Bade Sahab.; Real chemistry: –CH₃ → –COOH with hot KMnO₄ (needs benzylic H).

characters.name: Hostel warden → Bunty Uncle
characters.text: Makeover: Hostel warden → Bunty Uncle; What happens in the story: Tin or Iron with acid softens the warden into the loudest host.; Real chemistry: –NO₂ → –NH₂ with Sn/HCl or Fe/HCl.

characters.name: Bunty Uncle → germophobe
characters.text: Makeover: Bunty Uncle → germophobe; What happens in the story: He walks into a sour (acidic) room and turns cold.; Real chemistry: –NH₂ → –NH₃⁺ in acid.

characters.name: Bunty Uncle → married Bunty
characters.text: Makeover: Bunty Uncle → married Bunty; What happens in the story: Marriage (acetic anhydride) calms him.; Real chemistry: –NH₂ → –NHCOCH₃.

characters.name: Bunty Uncle leaves as smoke
characters.text: Makeover: Bunty Uncle leaves as smoke; What happens in the story: After guiding guests to their seats, he vanishes in a puff (N₂ gas) and anyone can take his seat.; Real chemistry: Diazotisation, then replacement (Sandmeyer, H₃PO₂, KI, water).

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: Bade Bhaiya (Aluminium Chloride), who swore never to marry (anhydrous AlCl₃)
characters.text: Character: Bade Bhaiya (Aluminium Chloride), who swore never to marry (anhydrous AlCl₃); Filmy quirk: Has arranged every wedding in the mohalla, still single. Separates a guest from a clingy partner and sends the guest into the haveli: "Main sirf rishte karwata hoon." Refuses houses run by germophobes (Bade Sahab, the warden) and gets stuck holding Bunty Uncle's hand. Hates water: a wet house ruins his work.; Real chemistry: Lewis acid catalyst. Makes R⁺, RCO⁺ or Cl⁺ from RCl, RCOCl or Cl₂ (Friedel–Crafts, chlorination) and is regenerated. Fails on nitrobenzene, benzoic acid and aniline; must be anhydrous.

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: Chhote Bhaiya (FeCl₃ / FeBr₃)
characters.text: Character: Chhote Bhaiya (FeCl₃ / FeBr₃); Filmy quirk: Bhaiya's younger brother, also unmarried. Only arranges halogen rishtas. Side job: turns Mummy ji's kitchen violet when he visits (phenol test).; Real chemistry: Lewis acid for halogenating benzene. Neutral FeCl₃ gives a violet colour with phenols.

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: The five-star banquet hall (Pt, Pd)
characters.text: Character: The five-star banquet hall (Pt, Pd); Filmy quirk: Hosts hydrogen weddings any time, even at room temperature. Never changes.; Real chemistry: Pt or Pd catalyse hydrogenation at room temperature.

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: The dharamshala (Ni)
characters.text: Character: The dharamshala (Ni); Filmy quirk: Also hosts hydrogen weddings, but only if you heat it up first.; Real chemistry: Ni needs 523–573 K for hydrogenation.

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: The tired pandit (Lindlar's catalyst; Pd on BaSO₄)
characters.text: Character: The tired pandit (Lindlar's catalyst; Pd on BaSO₄); Filmy quirk: Always stops the ceremony halfway: "Bas, aaj itna hi."; Real chemistry: Poisoned Pd: alkyne → cis-alkene only (Lindlar); acid chloride → aldehyde only (Rosenmund).

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: The sponsor (Hg²⁺)
characters.text: Character: The sponsor (Hg²⁺); Filmy quirk: Water and an alkyne won't meet unless he pays for the event.; Real chemistry: HgSO₄/dil. H₂SO₄ catalyses alkyne hydration (ethyne → acetaldehyde, others → ketones).

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: The bouncer (ZnCl₂ in the Lucas test)
characters.text: Character: The bouncer (ZnCl₂ in the Lucas test); Filmy quirk: Helps –OH get thrown out of a party. Throws out 3° guests at once, 2° in about five minutes, 1° not at all.; Real chemistry: ZnCl₂ helps –OH leave; turbidity speed shows 3°, 2° or 1° alcohol.

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: The strict principal (conc. H₂SO₄)
characters.text: Character: The strict principal (conc. H₂SO₄); Filmy quirk: Her decision depends on the room temperature: at 443 K she breaks the student's –OH and H off together (alkene); at 413 K she pairs two students (ether). Also arranges the fight that gives birth to Nitronium.; Real chemistry: Dehydrating acid: ethanol → ethene (443 K) or diethyl ether (413 K). With HNO₃ makes NO₂⁺. Catalyst in esterification.

characters.section: Catalysts: the bhaiyas who never marry, and friends
characters.name: Proton, the bechara catalyst (H⁺ in acid catalysis)
characters.text: Character: Proton, the bechara catalyst (H⁺ in acid catalysis); Filmy quirk: Starts the fight, then quietly takes his own place back at the end.; Real chemistry: H⁺ protonates first and is released again (dehydration, esterification, hydration of alkenes).

characters.name: Nitronium, the angry young man (NO₂⁺)
characters.text: Character: Nitronium, the angry young man (NO₂⁺); Filmy quirk: Born only when two tough acids fight in a dark gali. Always wants to barge in first: "Main sabse pehle!"; Real chemistry: Formed from conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄; attacks the ring in nitration.

characters.name: Proton, the bechara hero (H⁺)
characters.text: Character: Proton, the bechara hero (H⁺); Filmy quirk: "Mere paas kuch nahi hai." Owns nothing, wants electrons, always strikes first. Goes to the brother who is already rich: "jiske paas zyada, use aur."; Real chemistry: H⁺ is the first attacker in additions to C=C, and joins the carbon that already has more H (Markovnikov).

characters.name: The twins separated at birth (OH⁻ in water vs in alcohol)
characters.text: Character: The twins separated at birth (OH⁻ in water vs in alcohol); Filmy quirk: Same face, two lives. The twin raised in water (aq. KOH) is a straightforward attacker. The twin raised in alcohol (alc. KOH) is a pickpocket who steals a hydrogen from next door.; Real chemistry: Aqueous KOH: substitution (alcohol). Alcoholic KOH: elimination (alkene).

characters.name: Do-muha, the two-faced cousin (CN⁻; NO₂⁻)
characters.text: Character: Do-muha, the two-faced cousin (CN⁻; NO₂⁻); Filmy quirk: Whose side he takes depends on who he arrives with. With Potassium he shakes hands with his C side; with Silver he can only offer his N side. Brings one extra family member wherever he goes.; Real chemistry: KCN → nitrile (C attacks); AgCN → isocyanide (N attacks). Same pattern: KNO₂ → nitrite, AgNO₂ → nitro compound. CN adds one carbon.

characters.name: Bromine, the bahuroopiya (master of disguise)
characters.text: Character: Bromine, the bahuroopiya (master of disguise); Filmy quirk: Four disguises, one per story type: the attacker (electrophile in Br₂ addition), the second visitor (Br⁻ in HBr addition), the loner (Br• with peroxide), the one who walks out (leaving group). Always wears red-brown, and the colour vanishes when he meets a double bond.; Real chemistry: Bromine's four roles (H2, H3, H4, X1). Br₂ decolourising = test for unsaturation.

characters.name: The akela (radicals)
characters.text: Character: The akela (radicals); Filmy quirk: Loners with one unpaired electron. Each one steals a partner from someone else and leaves a new loner behind, so the story keeps going until two loners meet and settle down together. Only appear in light, heat, with Peroxide Pandit, or at Kolbe's electric shop.; Real chemistry: Radical chain: initiation, propagation, termination. Started by hν, heat, peroxide or electrolysis.

characters.name: Peroxide Pandit
characters.text: Character: Peroxide Pandit; Filmy quirk: Changes only one story: when he blesses HBr, Bromine arrives first in his loner disguise and the ending flips. He has no power over HCl or HI.; Real chemistry: Peroxide effect (anti-Markovnikov) for HBr only.

characters.name: Carbon Singh, the hero
characters.text: Character: Carbon Singh, the hero; Filmy quirk: Always keeps exactly four promises.; Real chemistry: Carbon is tetravalent.

characters.name: Carbon in crisis (carbocation)
characters.text: Character: Carbon in crisis (carbocation); Filmy quirk: Lost a partner and his electrons. Flat on the floor, insecure. Calms down only with bodyguards around: three bodyguards (3°) best, none (methyl) worst. If a richer relative lives next door, he quietly moves in there (rearrangement). Both doors open, so whoever comes next can enter from either side.; Real chemistry: Carbocation: planar, stability 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺, stabilised by alkyl groups; rearranges by 1,2-shift; SN1 gives both mirror images (racemisation).

characters.name: The goon with extra cash (carbanion)
characters.text: Character: The goon with extra cash (carbanion); Filmy quirk: Pushy, has extra electrons to spend. Feels best with few relatives around.; Real chemistry: Carbanion stability CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3°.

characters.name: The pushy goon who melts in water (Grignard reagent, RMgX)
characters.text: Character: The pushy goon who melts in water (Grignard reagent, RMgX); Filmy quirk: Tough, attacks any exposed carbon. But one drop of water and he's finished. Only works in the Dry Ether desert.; Real chemistry: RMgX attacks C=O and CO₂; destroyed by any acidic H; needs dry ether.

characters.name: Iodu Baba (I⁻)
characters.text: Character: Iodu Baba (I⁻); Filmy quirk: The easiest bidaai: "Theek hai, chalta hoon."; Real chemistry: I⁻ is the best halide leaving group.

characters.name: Bromo Bhai (Br⁻)
characters.text: Character: Bromo Bhai (Br⁻); Filmy quirk: Leaves with a little drama.; Real chemistry: Good leaving group.

characters.name: Chamku (Cl⁻)
characters.text: Character: Chamku (Cl⁻); Filmy quirk: Leaves only after a long argument.; Real chemistry: Moderate leaving group.

characters.name: Fiza, the bride who never leaves (F⁻)
characters.text: Character: Fiza, the bride who never leaves (F⁻); Filmy quirk: "Main kabhi nahi jaungi." No bidaai ever.; Real chemistry: C–F strongest; F⁻ the worst leaving group.

characters.name: –OH, the guest who won't leave unless offered tea
characters.text: Character: –OH, the guest who won't leave unless offered tea; Filmy quirk: Refuses to leave until someone hands her a Proton; then leaves happily as water.; Real chemistry: –OH leaves only after protonation (as H₂O) or conversion with SOCl₂/PCl₅/HX.

characters.name: The guest who leaves as smoke (N₂ from a diazonium salt)
characters.text: Character: The guest who leaves as smoke (N₂ from a diazonium salt); Filmy quirk: Lives only in the cold. Leaves in a puff of smoke, and anyone can take his seat.; Real chemistry: ArN₂⁺ stable only at 273–278 K; N₂ leaves as gas; replaced by Cl, Br, CN, I, F, OH or H.

characters.name: Daanveer Sodium, the hothead (Na)
characters.text: Character: Daanveer Sodium, the hothead (Na); Filmy quirk: Gives away his one electron instantly. Show him water and he explodes; kept in a kerosene jail. Takes the nervous hydrogen from alcohols and terminal alkynes, and joins two alkyl guests together.; Real chemistry: Na + water: violent, releases H₂. Na releases H₂ from O–H and ≡C–H. Wurtz reaction. Stored under kerosene.

characters.name: Potassium, the bigger hothead (K)
characters.text: Character: Potassium, the bigger hothead (K); Filmy quirk: Like Sodium, but explodes even faster. Mostly appears as the partner who decides the twins' and the two-faced cousin's behaviour.; Real chemistry: More reactive than Na. K⁺ salts: KOH, KCN, KNO₂.

characters.name: The rich daanveer (LiAlH₄)
characters.text: Character: The rich daanveer (LiAlH₄); Filmy quirk: Donates hydrogen gifts to almost everyone: aldehydes, ketones, acids, esters, amides, nitriles. Never to a plain double bond.; Real chemistry: Strong hydride donor; does not reduce isolated C=C.

characters.name: The choosy donor (NaBH₄)
characters.text: Character: The choosy donor (NaBH₄); Filmy quirk: Gives only to aldehydes and ketones.; Real chemistry: Mild hydride donor; does not reduce acids or esters.

characters.name: The polite boarder (B₂H₆)
characters.text: Character: The polite boarder (B₂H₆); Filmy quirk: Always sits at the less crowded end of a double bond, leaving the crowded end for Hydrogen.; Real chemistry: Hydroboration–oxidation gives the anti-Markovnikov alcohol.

characters.name: The purple saas (KMnO₄)
characters.text: Character: The purple saas (KMnO₄); Filmy quirk: Two moods. Cool mood: gives two aashirwaads and her purple fades. Hot mood: throws out every chamcha standing near the haveli and turns the man into Bade Sahab; tears double-bond couples apart. Can't touch a guest who has no chamche (tert-butyl).; Real chemistry: Cold dilute alkaline KMnO₄ adds two –OH (Baeyer's test, pink fades). Hot KMnO₄ oxidises side chains with benzylic H to –COOH and cleaves C=C.

characters.name: The strict examiner (acidified K₂Cr₂O₇)
characters.text: Character: The strict examiner (acidified K₂Cr₂O₇); Filmy quirk: Wears orange; changes to green when she passes someone. Passes 1° and 2° alcohols, fails every 3° one: "Tumhare paas ek bhi Ramu Kaka nahi hai."; Real chemistry: Oxidises 1° (to aldehyde, then acid) and 2° (to ketone) alcohols; 3° has no H on the carbinol carbon; Cr₂O₇²⁻ orange → Cr³⁺ green.

characters.name: The gentle tutor (PCC)
characters.text: Character: The gentle tutor (PCC); Filmy quirk: Takes a 1° alcohol only one class up, to aldehyde. Never further.; Real chemistry: PCC stops at the aldehyde.

characters.name: The tailor (CrO₂Cl₂)
characters.text: Character: The tailor (CrO₂Cl₂); Filmy quirk: Alters only Methyl uncle's outfit into an aldehyde kurta, nothing more.; Real chemistry: Étard: toluene → benzaldehyde.

characters.name: The kainchi (ozone)
characters.text: Character: The kainchi (ozone); Filmy quirk: Cuts a double-bond couple into two, with Zinc standing guard so nobody gets damaged further.; Real chemistry: Ozonolysis; Zn/H₂O stops further oxidation.

characters.name: The generous jeweller (Tollens')
characters.text: Character: The generous jeweller (Tollens'); Filmy quirk: Gives a silver mirror to every aldehyde, desi or videsi. Never to a ketone.; Real chemistry: All aldehydes (aromatic too) give a silver mirror; ketones don't.

characters.name: The fussy jeweller (Fehling's)
characters.text: Character: The fussy jeweller (Fehling's); Filmy quirk: Gives red only to desi (aliphatic) aldehydes. Turns away Benzaldehyde and every ketone.; Real chemistry: Aliphatic aldehydes give red Cu₂O; aromatic aldehydes and ketones don't.

characters.name: CID Iodine (I₂ + NaOH)
characters.text: Character: CID Iodine (I₂ + NaOH); Filmy quirk: Hunts for one fingerprint: a CH₃ right next to C=O (or one step away from it, as CH₃CH(OH)–). Found? Yellow alarm.; Real chemistry: Iodoform test: CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– gives yellow CHI₃.

characters.name: The sindoor detector (Br₂ in CCl₄)
characters.text: Character: The sindoor detector (Br₂ in CCl₄); Filmy quirk: Red-brown sindoor that disappears the moment it meets a double-bond couple.; Real chemistry: Decolourisation = unsaturation.

characters.name: The fizz test (NaHCO₃)
characters.text: Character: The fizz test (NaHCO₃); Filmy quirk: Bubbles only for true acids. Mummy ji (phenol) gets no fizz.; Real chemistry: Carboxylic acids release CO₂; phenols don't.

characters.name: The gatekeeper (Hinsberg's reagent)
characters.text: Character: The gatekeeper (Hinsberg's reagent); Filmy quirk: Sorts guests by how many N–H they carry: two (1°) get a pass that dissolves in alkali; one (2°) gets a pass that doesn't; none (3°) are ignored.; Real chemistry: 1° product soluble in alkali, 2° insoluble, 3° no reaction.

characters.name: The stink bomb (carbylamine: CHCl₃ + alc. KOH)
characters.text: Character: The stink bomb (carbylamine: CHCl₃ + alc. KOH); Filmy quirk: Goes off only for guests with two N–H (1° amines).; Real chemistry: Isocyanide smell: 1° amines only.

characters.name: The violet visitor (neutral FeCl₃)
characters.text: Character: The violet visitor (neutral FeCl₃); Filmy quirk: See Chhote Bhaiya: turns Mummy ji's kitchen violet.; Real chemistry: Phenol test.

characters.name: The orange-red stamp (2,4-DNP)
characters.text: Character: The orange-red stamp (2,4-DNP); Filmy quirk: Stamps every aldehyde and ketone. Ignores acids.; Real chemistry: Test for C=O.

characters.name: The cold gatekeeper (HNO₂)
characters.text: Character: The cold gatekeeper (HNO₂); Filmy quirk: Desi amine guests (aliphatic 1°) vanish as gas and leave an alcohol behind; Bunty Uncle (aniline) in the cold becomes the smoke guest (diazonium).; Real chemistry: 1° aliphatic amine → alcohol + N₂; aniline at 273–278 K → diazonium salt.

characters.name: Any ring substitution
characters.text: Reaction: Any ring substitution; Stock scene: A guest enters the haveli, the house goes into one second of chaos, then Ramu Kaka says "Main chalta hoon, malik" and leaves. Daadi: "Ghar kabhi nahi tootega."; What it means: Electrophile attacks, arenium ion forms, H⁺ leaves, aromaticity restored.

characters.name: Nitration
characters.text: Reaction: Nitration; Stock scene: Two tough acids fight in a dark gali; Nitronium is born and barges into the haveli.; What it means: HNO₃ + H₂SO₄ → NO₂⁺; nitration.

characters.name: Halogenation
characters.text: Reaction: Halogenation; Stock scene: Chhote Bhaiya pulls Chlorine away from his twin and walks him to the haveli; Bhaiya goes home unchanged.; What it means: FeCl₃ polarises Cl₂; Cl⁺ attacks; catalyst regenerated.

characters.name: Friedel–Crafts alkylation
characters.text: Reaction: Friedel–Crafts alkylation; Stock scene: Bade Bhaiya brings a Methyl guest. Trouble: the new guest is a host who invites more guests, so the haveli gets overcrowded. A long-chain guest may swap seats on the way (carbocation rearrangement).; What it means: R⁺ attacks; product is more reactive, so polysubstitution; rearrangement possible.

characters.name: Friedel–Crafts acylation
characters.text: Reaction: Friedel–Crafts acylation; Stock scene: Bade Bhaiya brings a snobbish cousin (acyl). Once inside, the cousin keeps others out, so only one enters.; What it means: RCO⁺ attacks; product deactivated, so monosubstitution.

characters.name: Bhaiya refuses
characters.text: Reaction: Bhaiya refuses; Stock scene: Bhaiya reaches the gate, sees Bade Sahab / the warden / Bunty Uncle at the door, and turns back.; What it means: No Friedel–Crafts on strongly deactivated rings or on aniline (N grabs AlCl₃).

characters.name: Sulphonation
characters.text: Reaction: Sulphonation; Stock scene: The paying guest moves in, but can be asked to leave if you heat with dilute acid.; What it means: Sulphonation is reversible.

characters.name: Bunty Uncle's party
characters.text: Reaction: Bunty Uncle's party; Stock scene: Bromine water arrives; Bunty Uncle invites guests to all three seats at once: white crowd. To control him, get him married first (acetylation), then bring guests.; What it means: Aniline + Br₂(aq) → 2,4,6-tribromoaniline; acetylate to get mono.

characters.name: Mummy ji's party
characters.text: Reaction: Mummy ji's party; Stock scene: Same as Bunty's: Bromine water fills all three seats; in CS₂ at low temperature, only one guest.; What it means: Phenol + Br₂(aq) → 2,4,6-tribromophenol; Br₂/CS₂ → mono (o/p).

characters.name: SN2
characters.text: Reaction: SN2; Stock scene: The attacker comes in through the back door while the leaver walks out the front, at the same moment. The house is turned inside out like an umbrella in the wind. Crowded houses (3°) can't be entered from the back.; What it means: One step, backside attack, inversion; 1° > 2° > 3°.

characters.name: SN1
characters.text: Reaction: SN1; Stock scene: The leaver walks out first. Carbon in crisis lies flat and calls his bodyguards. Then the attacker walks in, from front or back, so twins are born.; What it means: Two steps, carbocation, racemisation; 3° > 2° > 1°.

characters.name: Elimination
characters.text: Reaction: Elimination; Stock scene: The alcohol-raised twin picks the pocket of the house next door (a β-H), and the leaver walks out; the two neighbours become a double-bond couple.
